messages.subject: camtrapR version 0.99.7 released
messages.body_plain:
The new version of camtrapR (0.99.7) was released on CRAN.

Here's the news section of the new release:

Changes in camtrapR 0.99.7
==========================

bugfixes
------------
 o recordTable: returned station ID as camera ID if IDfrom = "metadata" and cameraID = "directory"

new features
------------
  o detectionMaps: gained argument 'backgroundPolgygon' for plotting a SpatialPolygon object in the background of the maps
  o imageRename: new argument 'createEmptyDirectories' to control whether empty directories should be copied or not
  o imageRename: if outDir contains images already, the function will not stop with an error, but asks you whether or not to copy new images (useful if data come in over time)

other changes
------------
  o recordTable / recordTableIndividual: improved handling and reporting of stations without images (warning instead of error)
  o recordTable / recordTableIndividual: improved handling and reporting of stations where all images lack species/individual metadata tags (only if using metadata ID, functions will throw warning instead of error)

There's also a new section about a possible issue with time zones and daylight saving time in vignette Date Extraction:
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/DataExtraction.html

In short: if you specify a time zone with daylight saving time, but your cameras don't record the time zone (and therefore don't use daylight saving time), records during DST will be off by 1 hour. In that case it's better to use the default UTC time zone.

messages.subject: Re: Any advise for exiftools in Windows 10?
messages.subject_clean: Any advise for exiftools in Windows 10?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bryn,
Normally, there should be no problems with Exiftool under Windows 10. Have you seen the section on Exiftool in the package vignette (see here <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/ImageOrganisation.html#exiftool>)?. You should download and install the Stand-alone installer (instruction can be found here <http://www.sno.phy.queensu.ca/~phil/exiftool/install.html#Windows>).

If your problem persists, please share the code you ran. Knowing which function caused the error will help find the problem quickly.

I'd like to add one thing to what Hugo said. It would be easier if you put exiftool.exe into a system directory (one of the directories contained in your PATH variable, e.g. C:/Windows). Windows (through R) will then be able to find Exiftool by default without the need to run these 2 lines in every R session.
And here's a second point: if you create an Exiftool directory in your image directory, don't put it into a directory next to your station directories (e.g. myStudy/renamed_images/Exiftool), but give it a directory of its own (e.g. .../myStudy/Exiftool). camtrapR would then assume that "Exiftool" is one of your stations.

Another potential problem is the Windows default of hiding known file extensions. In renaming Exiftool, one can inadvertedly rename exiftool.exe to exiftool.exe.exe (because the second .exe is hidden). It can be changed in the Windows folder options. See here <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/help/865219/how-to-show-or-hide-file-name-extensions-in-windows-explorer> for instructions.

Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: camtrapR version 0.99.7 released
messages.body_plain:
Dear Christy,
if you tag images in digiKam, these tags will be extracted and tabulated automatically by the function recordTable (and recordTableIndividual too). Assigning these tags is identical to species tagging. For example, create a tag group for Sex, and in it create 3 tags (male, female, unknown). The same goes for age class or other tags you may wish to assign.

Currently, I have no plans to include MCP plots in the package. That said, you can create them easily with the plotMCP function of the secr package. You need a capthist object, which is returned by spatialDetectionHistory.
See:
library(secr)
?plotMCP
example(plotMCP)

Regards,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Dear Jess,
all I can say at this point is that this should not be happening and very clearly is a bug. It seems to have to do with assigning the camera ID in the output table, but I'm not sure yet. Would you please provide the output of sessionInfo()? And the directory structure of the station directory that caused the trouble? If possible, I'd appreciate very much if you could dropbox me that directory (or a subset thereof) via email for me to reproduce, understand and then fix the problem, as I haven't seen it before.
Also, does the function copy anything at all?

Normally, folders within folders should be no problem, as the software will recursively find all JPG images in subdirectories. And manually having to move directories is something that camtrapR was meant to render unnecessary, so I hope I'll be able to provide a solution soon.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error with Function spatiaDetectionHistory- entities in stationCol do not match.
messages.subject_clean: Error with Function spatiaDetectionHistory- entities in stationCol do not match.
messages.body_plain:
Dear Aditya,

what the function does internally when it returns this error is:

if(!all(recordTableIndividual$Station %in% CTtable$Station)) stop ("there are entries in stationCol of recordTableIndividual that are not found in stationCol of CTtable")

in plain English: If not all stations in recordTableIndividual are found in CTtable$Station, throw an error. These functions are quite reliable normally, and will complain at the slightest difference, like a conflict between upper/lower case or an "invisible" space behind a station name.

You can try this on your data:

any(!data$Station %in% CtTb$Station)    # is any value of data$Station NOT in CtTb$Station?
which(!data$Station %in% CtTb$Station)  # which value of data$Station is NOT in CtTb$Station?

data$Station[which(!data$Station %in% CtTb$Station)]  # show that value in data
CtTb$Station[which(!CtTb$Station %in% data$Station)]  # show that value in CtTb

# i used these fake data for testing:
data <- data.frame(Station = c("A", "B", "C"))
CtTb <- data.frame(Station = c("A", "B", "C "))

Does this help?
Jürgen
